A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Moscat research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, appendices and checklists. Matching relocated material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original node-classification experiments, ablations, runtime measurements and expert-behavior analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Independent scope-expert training, holdout-based attention gating, heterophily-biased filtering and scope-aware logit augmentation remain unchanged. The added memory analysis describes the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same node-classification coverage: eight main benchmarks, with Chameleon and PubMed also used in the appendices. The relocated depth comparison uses existing datasets and scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain their GNN, Graph Transformer, Graph MoE, skip-connection and ensemble baselines. GAMLP and ACMGCN already participated in v3's appendix depth comparison before its relocation into v4's main text.

E3.justification: The two Moscat evaluation setups, data splits, preprocessing, accuracy/ROC-AUC metrics, depth ranges and experimental hyperparameters are retained. The new sequential-versus-parallel memory discussion does not report changed experimental execution.

E4.justification: The component ablations and depth, dropout, hidden-dimension, training-epoch, filtering, embedding, overlap and gating-weight studies are retained. Moving the depth comparison into Section 5.2 does not add an experiment; the new space bounds are theoretical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten runs per dataset in Appendix F.1 and identify the reported uncertainty as standard deviation in checklist item 7. No run-count, seed or statistical-reporting changes are introduced.

E6.justification: Tabulated results and plotted data are unchanged. However, v3 Appendix G.3 describes GAMLP/ACMGCN improving through 4 layers and then stabilizing, while v4 Section 5.2 describes gains through 4–6 layers. This is a limited revision of a reported trend, without evidence of new runs.

T1.justification: New Appendix G.3 derives space-complexity bounds for sequential expert training, parallel expert training and gating-model training, including linear versus quadratic dependence on maximum depth. The existing generalization assumptions, Theorem 3.3 and Appendix B proof are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about depth-dependent generalization disparities, decoupled expert gating, architectural flexibility and superior benchmark performance.

C2.justification: v4 adds an explicit runtime–memory tradeoff: parallel expert training at comparable runtime requires approximately Lmax times the memory of one deepest expert, while sequential training reduces memory requirements. v3's runtime discussion lacked this qualification.

D1.justification: Appendix G.3 newly documents sequential and parallel training options and their memory requirements, adding practical resource-planning guidance. Existing software versions, hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 removes Gomes et al. (2024), 'Depth scaling in graph neural networks: Understanding the flat curve behavior,' and the associated citation in the depth discussion. The broader related-work coverage and research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The depth discussion is condensed and moved into Section 5.2, appendix subsections are renumbered, and acknowledgments and author/conference information are updated. Local wording and notation edits include correcting Equation 25, but four Moscat references become undefined 'AH' references.

P2.justification: v3's appendix Figure 8 becomes v4's main-text Figure 5, with accompanying caption edits and reflow of other figures and tables. All original displays are retained. Appendix pagination now splits the gating-weight discussion across intervening figures and a mostly empty page 37.

improvement.justification: The added space analysis improves resource transparency by explaining the memory cost behind parallel-training runtime claims, which v3 did not address explicitly. Promoting the existing depth comparison improves access to relevant evidence. These modest benefits are partly offset by undefined 'AH' references and awkward appendix pagination.
